OpenShift / Kubernetes

Pod health, deployments, warning events, pod logs and CPU and memory usage on OpenShift and Kubernetes clusters

Docs / Integrations / Build, release and runtime / OpenShift / Kubernetes

Area
toil openshift
Status
unitShipped, with its logic tested against stubbed HTTP. Never run against a real instance.
Credential
Service account token
Env prefix
TOIL_OPENSHIFT_
Supports
Not yet established

skills/toil/openshift.md

Pod health, Deployments and DeploymentConfigs, warning events, pod logs, and CPU and memory usage for one namespace, read from the cluster’s API server over REST. Every command reads; none changes anything. There’s no kubeconfig and no other CLI involved. Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: The oldest OpenShift / Kubernetes version toil supports hasn’t been established. pods, events and logs use core v1; deployments uses apps/v1, or apps.openshift.io/v1 for DeploymentConfigs; pod-metrics and resource-usage need metrics-server (metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1). No release has been verified yet.

Credential

A Bearer token, typically a service account token with read access to the namespaces you’ll ask about. The OpenShift web console’s Copy login command shows a token for your own user; for anything long-lived, create a service account token. toil sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token> to the connection’s baseUrl and nowhere else.

Configuration

One connection per cluster.

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_OPENSHIFT_BASE_URLyesAPI server URL, e.g. https://openshift.imagile.dev
tokenTOIL_OPENSHIFT_TOKENyesBearer token
envTOIL_OPENSHIFT_ENVnoEnvironment name --env selects this cluster by, e.g. prod
instanceTOIL_OPENSHIFT_INSTANCEnoCluster instance name --instance selects this cluster by, e.g. east

There’s no CI fallback variable. TOIL_OPENSHIFT_* sets the default connection; any other connection takes TOIL_CONN_<NAME>_*.

export TOIL_OPENSHIFT_BASE_URL=https://openshift.imagile.dev
export TOIL_OPENSHIFT_TOKEN=<your token>

Several clusters, in ~/.toil/config.json:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "prod-east": { "area": "openshift", "baseUrl": "https://api.prod-east.openshift.imagile.dev:6443", "env": "prod", "instance": "east" },
    "dev-east": { "area": "openshift", "baseUrl": "https://api.dev-east.openshift.imagile.dev:6443", "env": "dev", "instance": "east" }
  },
  "defaults": { "openshift": { "connection": "prod-east" } }
}

The token never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add prod-east --area openshift (or toil connections login prod-east) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_CONN_PROD_EAST_TOKEN.

Choosing a cluster

--env <name> and --instance <name> go on the group (toil openshift --env prod --instance east pods ...) or after the command. Each picks the connection with that name, or the one whose env (or instance) setting matches. Given together, they must pick the same connection. When a value matches several, the other flag narrows it: with two prod clusters, --env prod --instance east picks the one that is both, while --env prod alone is an INVALID_INPUT naming them, so add --instance or use --connection <name>. An unknown name is an INVALID_INPUT listing the clusters toil knows. With neither flag, the default connection is used (defaults.openshift.connection, else the one named openshift, else the only one).

Where the contract nests clusters in an openshift.environments.<env>.instances.<instance> map, toil has one connection per cluster with env and instance set. The contract’s defaultEnvironment and defaultInstance are defaults.openshift.connection, and its flat baseUrl and token are a connection with neither set.

A cluster with env and instance set reports a missing baseUrl or token as OpenShift cluster "<env>/<instance>" is not configured or missing baseUrl. or ... is missing a token.; one without them as OpenShift not configured. or OpenShift credentials not configured., all NOT_CONFIGURED.

Commands

Every command but cluster list needs --namespace <ns>.

  • cluster list: Lists every configured cluster: it runs toil connections list --area openshift (CLI only; over MCP, call the connections_list tool with area openshift). Each connection shows its name, isDefault, host, writes and where each setting came from, never a secret. It takes no --env or --instance.
  • pods: Pod health summary: phase counters, crashLoopBackOff, imagePullBackOff (which includes ErrImagePull), oomKilled and totalRestarts, then each pod with phase, ready, restartCount, age, reason, message, containers and labels. Failed pods come first, then Pending, then Unknown, then the rest, by restarts within each. --label-selector filters; --raw returns the pod objects unmodified, with count.
  • deployments: Deployments (apps/v1), or DeploymentConfigs (apps.openshift.io/v1) with --deployment-configs: ready as ready/desired, replica counts, age, images, strategy, latestVersion, and only the problem conditions (Available or Progressing that are False, and any ReplicaFailure), sorted by unavailable replicas. --raw returns the objects unmodified.
  • events: Warning events only, unless --all. --field-selector adds to the type=Warning selector, joined with a comma. Sorted by count, highest first.
  • logs: The last --lines (default 100) lines of --pod’s log, as text in log. --container picks a container; without it no container is sent, and the API server refuses a pod with more than one unless it names a default container. --previous reads the previous container instance.
  • pod-metrics: Each pod’s containers with their raw cpu and memory usage, from metrics-server.
  • resource-usage: One row per container: usage, limits and requests, in millicores (m) and mebibytes (Mi); a quantity toil can’t read is null. --csv --out <file> also writes the rows as CSV to a new file inside the workspace (it never overwrites) and returns its absolute path as file. --csv needs --out, and --out needs --csv. The CSV header is Pod,Container,CPU Usage (m),Memory Usage (Mi),CPU Limits (m),Memory Limits (Mi),CPU Requests (m),Memory Requests (Mi), with an empty cell for null.

Lists come back whole: the API server is asked for everything in one response, with no paging.

toil openshift pods --namespace payments
toil openshift --env prod --instance east events --namespace payments --all
toil openshift logs --namespace payments --pod api-7d9f8b6c5-abcde --container api --lines 50
toil openshift resource-usage --namespace payments --csv --out usage.csv

Checking a dossier

check-dossier checks the call’s dossier for the call’s environment (--env, else the dossier’s own) against that environment’s cluster: each namespace it names (namespace, namespaces) is a project the token can see, and each deployment in deployments exists in its namespace. With one namespace per repo, a deployment passes when any of them has it, and the check’s note says where it was looked for. It’s toil openshift check-dossier (--dossier <name|file>, or the dossier the folder resolves to), and it returns { dossier, connection, env, ok, checked, checks, unchecked }, one check per value with its key path. The CLI exits 1 when one is missing. A failure other than not-found (a bad token, an unreachable host) fails the command. Read only.

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl

    API server URL, e.g. https://openshift.imagile.dev

    TOIL_OPENSHIFT_BASE_URL

  • token secret

    Bearer token, typically a service account token

    TOIL_OPENSHIFT_TOKEN

  • env

    Environment name that --env selects this cluster by, e.g. prod

    TOIL_OPENSHIFT_ENV

  • instance

    Cluster instance name within the environment that --instance selects this cluster by, e.g. east

    TOIL_OPENSHIFT_INSTANCE

Commands at a glance

  • toil openshiftpods

    List pod health summary for a namespace — pre-processed for LLM analysis. Use --raw to return the full unmodified Kubernetes pod objects.

    MCP openshift_pods--namespace <ns>--label-selector <selector>--raw--env <name>--instance <name>

  • toil openshiftdeployments

    List Deployments (or OpenShift DeploymentConfigs with --deployment-configs) for a namespace, read-only. Use --raw to return the full unmodified objects.

    MCP openshift_deployments--namespace <ns>--label-selector <selector>--deployment-configs--raw--env <name>--instance <name>

  • toil openshiftevents

    List Warning events for a namespace — pre-filtered for LLM analysis

    MCP openshift_events--namespace <ns>--field-selector <selector>--all--env <name>--instance <name>

  • toil openshiftlogs

    Get recent log lines from a pod container

    MCP openshift_logs--namespace <ns>--pod <name>--container <name>--lines <n>--previous--env <name>--instance <name>

  • toil openshiftpod-metrics

    Get CPU and memory usage for pods in a namespace (requires metrics-server)

    MCP openshift_pod_metrics--namespace <ns>--env <name>--instance <name>

  • toil openshiftresource-usage

    Combined CPU/memory usage, limits, and requests for all pods in a namespace — all values normalized to millicores (m) and mebibytes (Mi). Requires metrics-server. Use --csv with --out <file> to also save a spreadsheet-friendly CSV.

    MCP openshift_resource_usage--namespace <ns>--label-selector <selector>--csv--out <file>--env <name>--instance <name>

  • toil openshiftcheck-dossier

    Check the call's dossier against OpenShift: its namespaces and deployments exist

    MCP openshift_check_dossier--env <name>--instance <name>
